Life of an access request · 2026 edition

      
An AI agent asks for access. Here is everything that should happen next.

    

    

      

        
        agent://invoice-assistant
        
      

      
    
        
  1. 01
    Discover
    The agent is in the inventory, with a named human owner and a purpose. No shadow agents.
    2. 
        
  2. 02
    Authenticate
    Workload identity and a short-lived token. No passwords, no API key pasted into a prompt.
    3. 
        
  3. 03
    Authorize
    Least privilege, just in time. Read invoices, yes. Change bank details, no.
    4. 
        
  4. 04
    Approve
    High-impact actions pause for a human, with the agent's intent shown in plain words.
    5. 
        
  5. 05
    Audit
    Every call is logged against the agent and its owner, reviewed and certified like any other access.
    6.

    The identity gap
      
        
      Controls that close it
        
      
        
      
        Measure it by 
        
    
        
  
        

  
        
    
        Public record The same lessons, from real incidents
        
    
        
      
        2024
        
        Snowflake customer data theft
        
        
        Attackers used credentials stolen by infostealer malware to sign in to customer accounts that had no MFA. Mandiant notified about 165 potentially exposed organisations.
        
        Lesson: phishing-resistant MFA everywhere, and rotate what may have leaked.
        Google Cloud · Mandiant ↗
              
      
        2024
        
        Midnight Blizzard at Microsoft
        
        
        A password spray hit a legacy, non-production test account without MFA. From there the actor used a legacy OAuth application with elevated access.
        
        Lesson: forgotten accounts and app identities are still identities. Inventory and retire them.
        Microsoft Security Response Center ↗
              
      
        2025
        
        Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report
        
        
        Credential abuse remained a leading way in, and breaches involving a third party doubled to 30% in one year.
        
        Lesson: every partner, integration and agent connection is part of your identity surface.
        Verizon DBIR 2025 ↗

        The playbook
        
      
        Six controls for agentic identity.
        
      
          
        
        1. Find every identity. People, service accounts, API keys and agents, in one inventory.
          2. 
        
        2. Give every agent an owner. A named human answers for what it can do.
          3. 
        
        3. Least privilege, just in time. Access that is scoped, conditional and expires.
          4. 
        
        4. No standing secrets. Short-lived tokens and vaulted, rotated keys.
          5. 
        
        5. Humans approve high-impact actions. Money, data exports and access changes pause for a person.
          6. 
        
        6. Log it, review it, certify it. Agents join the same access reviews as everyone else.
          7.
